title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages. Pi is a (punctured) curve or surface. pi is its fundamental group (discrete or profinite). Script-T (transcribed 'Gamma' here) is a set with a pi-action; it is plausibly the set of cusps or 'points at infinity' viewed in the universal cover, i.e. a set of conjugate inertia subgroups. Sigma is an extension 1 -> pi -> Sigma -> G -> 1 (typically G is a Galois group) acting on (script-T, pi). For each t, the stabilizer pi_t is abelian and canonically isomorphic to a fixed group T (think Zhat(1), or Z with an orientation). G acts on T through a character chi (cyclotomic-type).

Previous page. The action groupoid <script-T, pi> has objects t in script-T and arrows lambda in pi with lambda t = t'. All its vertex groups are identified with T, making it a 'T-groupoid', on which Sigma acts compatibly, acting on T via G and chi.

This page.
(1) Since G acts on T, each t yields an injective homomorphism phi(t): T ~ pi_t into pi. This gives a map phi: script-T -> Hom_gr(T, pi). It is pi-equivariant, with pi acting on the target by conjugation: phi(lambda t) = int(lambda) o phi(t). It is also Sigma-equivariant up to the twist by chi. In modern terms, this is the family of canonical generators of the cuspidal inertia groups.
(2) There is a homomorphism of groupoids from <script-T, pi> to the groupoid of universal coverings of Pi. Every object goes to the (unpointed) universal cover Pi~, whose automorphism group is pi. On arrows it is the inclusion pi_{t,t'} := Isom(t,t') = {lambda in pi : lambda t = t'} ⊂ pi. This is the canonical faithful functor from the action groupoid to the one-object groupoid Bpi; it is in fact a covering of groupoids (discrete fibration). It is compatible with the Sigma-actions (on Pi~ and on pi).
(3) The next page states the converse. From a T-groupoid Lambda with a Sigma-action and a faithful, Sigma-compatible functor Lambda -> <pi> (equivalently a family of subgroups pi_t and bitransporter sets), one reconstructs script-T := Ob Lambda as a Sigma-set together with the cuspidal data.

Purpose. To give an intrinsic, groupoid-theoretic encoding of 'fundamental group of a curve together with its peripheral (cusp) structure and the outer Galois action'. This is part of the combinatorial and anabelian 'paradigms' of algebraic curves pursued in the Esquisse/Longue Marche period.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. One caveat: 'antihomomorphisme' is almost certainly a misreading. phi is a map of sets, equivariant for conjugation, not a homomorphism, since script-T is only a set.

The functor from the action groupoid to Bpi is faithful, and in fact a covering of groupoids. The next page generalizes it to arbitrary faithful functors, which correspond to more general data than pi-sets (subgroup families plus bitransporters). The distinction is noted but not worked out on this page.

ideas.what: Map script-T -> Hom(T, pi) assigning to each cusp the canonical embedding of T ≅ inertia group; equivariant for pi-conjugation and for Sigma via chi
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal inertia subgroups with canonical (cyclotomic) generators; peripheral structure of a surface group
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (SGA1 tame fundamental group); anabelian formulations by Nakamura, Mochizuki, Hoshi-Mochizuki (1990s-2000s)
ideas.where_published: Inertia and tame ramification appear in SGA1/SGA7; the cusp-structured formulation is implicit in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche

ideas.what: The action groupoid <script-T, pi> with all vertex groups identified with a fixed abelian group T ('T-groupoid'), with a semi-linear Sigma-action twisted by chi
ideas.modern_name: action groupoid / groupoid with trivialized abelian band; twisted equivariant structure (cf. band/lien)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Groupoid formalism: Grothendieck/Giraud (bands); application to cusps: anabelian literature
ideas.where_published: Related notions of liens in Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne; fundamental groupoids with base-point sets in Esquisse and Longue Marche

ideas.what: Faithful functor from the action groupoid to the groupoid of universal covers (Bpi), and the converse: data equivalent to a faithful Sigma-compatible functor from a T-groupoid
ideas.modern_name: covering of groupoids / discrete fibration over Bpi (Grothendieck construction for pi-sets)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (Galois categories, fibre functors); general groupoid language in Pursuing Stacks

deep.surprise_reason: This page is routine bookkeeping: the action groupoid of cusps, canonical inertia embeddings, and the faithful functor to Bpi with a Galois-twisted action. It is a careful, intrinsic formalization of peripheral structure, but every ingredient is standard. Equivalent formalisms appear in later anabelian work.
transcription_corrections: 'Γ' throughout should be script-T (𝒯), the same set as on the previous page, not Gamma.
'donne naissance [?] à un antihomomorphisme [?]' is more plausibly 'donne naissance automatiquement [à une application]' or similar; it is not an antihomomorphism.

'consistant [?] en les objets à valeurs Π̃ sur ceux-ci, équivalence [?] dans l'ens. des flèches dans π' likely reads 'consistant à envoyer les objets sur Π̃, et en l'inclusion dans l'ens. des flèches dans π'.
'on l'inclusion' should read 'on a l'inclusion' of pi_{t,t'} into pi.
The crossed-out text above pi_{t,t'} reads 'Isom_{<𝒯,π>}', with '(t,t')' added above it.
